answer: Randomized seat assignment. Each epoch, a public beacon emits a verifiable random value; identities are hashed with it and mapped onto a fixed capacity knoll of active slots, ordered toward a summit of influence and a nadir of dormant positions. Attackers cannot precompute placement, since the beacon is unknown at registration. To occupy many slots, an adversary must register many identities and repeatedly win the random draw; each identity carries an ongoing rent plus the cost of maintaining liveness through unknown future placements.
